Problem 1¶

Points: 20

In this problem we will use data on infidelity, known as the Fair's Affairs dataset. The Affairs dataset is available as part of the datasets package instatsmodels. This data comes from a survey conducted by Psychology Today in 1969, see Greene (2003) and Fair (1978) for more information.

The dataset contains various self-reported characteristics of 6366 participants, including how often the respondent engaged in extramarital sexual intercourse during the past year, as well as their gender, age, year married, whether they had children, their religiousness (on a 5-point scale, from 1=anti to 5=very), education, occupation (Hillingshead 7-point classification with reverse numbering), and a numeric self-rating of their marriage (from 1=very unhappy to 5=very happy).

(a) Describe the participants. Use descriptive, summarization, and exploratory techniques to describe the participants in the study. Tell us the average/mean of children count ? What is the average age of respondents? In your response comment on any ethical and privacy concerns you have with this dataset.

A) After conducting an exploratory analysis on the participants from this study, I know that the average count of children is 1.39 and that the average age of the respondents are 29 years old. I also know that the max age of respondents is 42 and the minimum age was 17.5. On average, the respondents from this survey have been married for 9 years with a self-rating of 4.10 on their marriage meaning that the average participant from this survey would be considered happy in their marriage. The average occurance of affairs from the respondents was 0.7 and ~32.24% of total respondent participants did engage in an affair. This brings up ethical and privacy concerns for me regarding the data and the participants. Was there privacy when the survey was being taken? I.e., spouse not in the same room or taking the same survey. The lack of privacy could affect or skew the data integrity of the results because participants could be swayed to answer untruthfully. On this same notion, because these metrics were self-rated; the scale in which someone decides may differ either substaintially or possibily very little from each other making it also difficult to asses the accuracy of the data. But particularly on the affairs metric, is it measured by "how often" they engaged in extramarital sexual intercourse or "time spent"? Either way, this can be seen as an invasion to privacy because an affair would be considered unethical and immoral in normative ethics, so is it ethical to be asking people to divulge this information?

(b) Suppose we want to explore the characteristics of participants who engage in extramarital sexual intercourse (i.e. affairs). Instead of modeling the number of affairs, consider the binary outcome - had an affair versus didn't have an affair. Create a new variable to capture this response variable of interest. What might the advantages and disadvantages of this approach to modeling the data be in this context?

1B) Some advantages into using a binary outcome approach like this is it easily splits your data into yes or no categories for a specific variable which can be useful for quick overviews and basic analysis like obtaining counts, grouping other variables together like had_affair and religion. It can also simplify creating data visualizations having these categories split into a yes or no. However, some disadvantages to this approach is it can disreagrd other nuances to your data that isn't easily seperated to yes or no categories or it oversimplifies data that is meant to be complex. For example, in this context, if I am looking at the data that is had an affair, that was converted into a value of "1" taking away the actual measurement of time/ frequency. When we are trying to see what other variables are creating a possible relationship, knowing exact measurements can create a stronger relationship to that varaible rather than just a one off e.g., someone who had an affair once vs someone who repeatedly had affairs and the relationship with children; having children or not having children could be a factor for number of occurances. Or how that can affect how the marriage rate is rated, is someone who often has affairs happy in their marriage or not? We can get an overview with the yes or no category, but having the data in the original form (in this context) would allow for a deeper dive in exploratory data analysis.

(c) Use an appropriate regression model to explore the relationship between having an affair (binary) and other personal characteristics. Comment on which covariates seem to be predictive of having an affair and which do not.

1C) In problem set 7 4b, I used gen ai to help me understand what my results summary were and the statistical significance, it was from that that I was able to understand that smaller p-values indicate a statistical significance with the variables. Hence the variables that seem to indicate a relationship with having an affair or not are age, years married, and religion. Because of the small p-values, these variables are statistically significant in this analysis and whether or not someone has children and their education do not seem to be predictive variables of whether or not someone has an affair.

(e) Interpret the model parameters using the model from part (d).

1E) Interpreting the model parameters from part 1D, as noted above, the variables that were included for this "best" fit model is rate_marriage, age, and years married. From the variables that were included all of them appear to be statistically significant because of the very small p-values = 0.000. The variable that seems to have a positive relationship to the variable of having had an affair is the number of years married; as the years increased so does the probability based on the positive coefficient. Because the other parameters are negative, as those increase, the probability of having an affair decreases. For example, as an individual gets older the liklihood of them having an affair decreases.

(f) Create an artificial test dataset where martial rating varies from 1 to 5 randomly and all other variables are set to their means. Use this artificial dataset as your test dataset to obtain predicted probabilities of having an affair for case in the test data. Interpret your results and use a visualization to support your interpretation.

1F) Interpreting my results from this artificial dataset, It is notable that the lower that a marriage was rated the probability of them having an affair is substainstially increased. Those indicating that they rated their marriage a 1 = very poor have a 79% probability of having an affair. And as the rate of the marriage increases the probability also decreases. My interpretation is supported in my visualization as you can see a clear linear relationship to increased probability with a low marriage rating and probability decreases the higher the marriage is rated.

(g) Reflect on your analysis in this problem. After completing all the parts of this analysis what remaining and additional ethical and privacy conerns do you have?

1G) After completing my analysis on this problem set 1, I have some doubts on my accuary of the models because originally when I ran the model I got the same variables with the same values. This didn't seem right so I changed the k_feature to only 3 variables and in doing so, the model parameter values also changed. I think some additional ethical concerns I have is that this model does not take into account the ethical principles and moral values that some people whole heartedly strive to uphold. Some people religous or not, would never harm their partner by cheating on them even if they are unhappy in their marriage. So this model discredits that and I also think this is not something that should be tried to be predicted.

Problem 2¶

Points: 20

In this problem set, we will use some data from a sports context. The data is provided as part of the Introduction to Statistial Learning with Applications in Python textbook. It was taken from the StatLib library which is maintained at Carnegie Mellon University. The data provided is part of the data that was used in the 1988 ASA Graphics Section Poster Session. The salary data were originally from Sports Illustrated, April 20, 1987. The 1986 and career statistics were obtained from The 1987 Baseball Encyclopedia Update published by Collier Books, Macmillan Publishing Company, New York.

Following the directions below to load this data, Hitters directly from the ISLP python package. You may need to install the ISLP package before you can get started. In the Jupyter Hub you can open a terminal and use pip install ISLP. Next load the data as follows:

(b) Briefly summarize the dataset, describing what data exists and its basic properties. Comment on any issues that need to be resolved before you can proceed with your analysis.

2B) In the Hitters dataset, it is a fairly small dataset with only 322 rows of data with 20 variables that hold information regarding baseball statistics such as home runs, at bats, hits and leauge info. It also contains salary information which is also the only column that contains some missing data values and is in a float dtype. The rest of the dataset is primarly integers and a few category types used to describe the division, league, and new leaugue info. Because the question I am striving to answer in my analysis has to do with the salary in which we have missing values, I am going to be dropping those NaN values so I do not get any issues or errors.

(c) Use the dataset to provide empirical evidence that addressed your question from (a). Discuss your results. Provide at least two visualizations to support your story.

2C) The question I was striving to answer was that does an increase in the number of years reflect an increase in salary amount? I decided to start with a scatter plot that plotted the number of years and salary information after having dropped the null values, and in this analysis I also added a regression line and found that the line is not well fitted. The data points in this graph show no true relationship with increased number of years and increased salary information. I decided then to group this information by the averages in which I found that up until getting to the mark of around 10 years, salary does appear to gradually increase however after that 10 year mark, as years keep increasing pay either increases or decreases, confirming once again that there is not a relationship between those 2 variables. I wanted to create another visualization that didn't group by the averages but rather a range of years. This was something I had done in ps8 in which problem 1C made note of the gen ai reference to help me group by these bins. In the last violin plot visualization was my final confirmation that the relationship could be considered non-existent. At least with the data that I had to work with, perhaps if there was more data, my results could be different. I logically would have assumed that as number of years increase so does salary, but it does not.

Problem 3¶

Points: 20

In this problem, we will use data available in Machine Learning with R by Brett Lantz. This data was available in the public domain and a few version exist online.

The data describe individual medical costs billed by health insurance. For each observation, there is information about:

  • age: age of primary beneficiary of the insurance policy
  • sex: the person's sex, measured here a binary gender
  • bmi: body mass index, providing an understanding of body, weights that are relatively high or low relative to height, (kg / m ^ 2)
  • children: number of children/dependents covered by health insurance
  • smoker: smoking status of the primary beneficiary
  • region: the beneficiary's residential area in the US, northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest.
  • charges: medical costs billed by health insurance

In our analysis, we will be interested in the relationship between charges and the individual characteristics measured.

(a) Examine the bivariate relationships present in the data. Briefly discuss notable results.

3A) After examining the data and looking at the bivariate relationships with the individual characteristics some notable results is how individuals who smoke have significantly higher charges than someone who does not. Another notable relationship is bmi. Individuals with higher bmi scores appear to have higher charges than someone who does not. Lastly, the last notable relationship is age, it appears that the older that someone is, the larger the charges as well.

(b) Fit a multiple linear regression model. How much variance in the medical costs(charges) does this variable- bmi explain?

3B) After fitting a multiple linear regression model, I calculated the variance by subtracting the r-squared values from the r-squared value that included bmi as a predictor and then subtracting it from the r-squared values that did not include bmi as a predictor to get the numerical measure of how spread out the values were. The BMI variance I calculated was 0.025 which is equivalent to 2.5% which is a small percentage indicating a not so strong relationship as bmi being a predictor to medical costs aka weak relationship.

Problem 5¶

Points: 10

Please answer the questions below by writing a short response.

(a) Describe three real-life applications in which classification might be useful. Describe the response, as well as the predictors. Is the goal in each application inference or predictions? Explain your answer.

5A) Referencing the class textbook ISLP_Python (pg. 135 & 136), we learned why using classification is important; we sometimes need to make predictions for responses that are classified as qualitative rather than quantitative. Three-real life applications that the textbook used was 1. A person arriving at the ER that is displaying a set of symptoms that could be one of three medical conditions. In this scenario the response variable would be the medical condition we are trying to pinpoint and the predictors would be the set of symptoms they are displaying. For this scenario, the goal for this application would be predition because we are trying to predict which medical condition the individual has based on a set of symptoms. 2. An online banking service trying to determine whether a transaction is fradulent or not based on IP address, past transaction histroy, etc. Similarly to the first scenario, this would also be a scenario where the goal is to predict because of the data the online banking service is able to use and see e.g., IP address, transaction history, etc. The response variable would be if the transaction is fradulent and the predictors would be the data that the banking service has. 3. The last example used was on a basis of DNA sequence data on patients that have and do not have a disease and a biologist is trying to see which DNA mutations are disease-causing and which ones are not. This example is a little different than the previous two because in this scenario the biologist is interested in more than just if someone has the disease or not so the goal in this application would be inference. In this application, the response variable is whether the DNA mutation is disease-causing and the predictors would be the DNA sequence data from the patients.

b) Describe three real-life applications in which regression might be useful. Describe the response, as well as the predictors. Is the goal in each application inference or predictions? Explain your answer.

5B) Three real-life applications in which regression might be useful is like the advertising budget and sales example in the ISLP_Python textbook, businesses can use regression to forecast sales. The goal in this example would be for prediction and the response variable would be sales and the predictor would be the advertising spend. Another example the text used is to predict credit balances using variables like income and student status. In this scenario, the response variable would be the credit card balance and the predictors are the income and student status, the goal in this application would also be prediction. Lastly, referencing an example from the course lab homeworks we could use regression to predict which individuals would be at high risk for heart disease. The response variable would be heart disease or not and the predictors would be the demographic information of the individuals or other factors like lifestyle and family history this could be prediction or inference. These are three real-life applications where regression is used in everday life and can be very insightful and valuable information.

(c) What are the advantages and disadvantages of a very flexible (versus a less flexible) approach for regression or classification? Under what circumstances might a more flexible approach be preferred to a less flexible approach? When might a less flexible approach be preferred?

5C) Some advantages of a very flexible approach is that it can capture complex relationships and since they are very flexible they are also adaptable. According to our ISLP (pg. 33) text book, more flexible methods also result in less bias. A disadvantage to that is there runs a risk of overfitting the data since the data is complex. An advantage to a less flexible approach is that they are more simple meaning less complex so they are easier to understand and there is a lower risk of overfitting the data, but runs a higher risk of bias which is a disadvantage. (Additional Reference: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/machine-learning/underfitting-and-overfitting-in-machine-learning/)

Problem 6¶

Points: 10

Suppose we have a dataset with five predictors, $X_1 =$ GPA, $X_2 =$ IQ, $X_3 =$ Gender (1 for Female, and 0 for Male), $X_4 =$ Interaction between GPA and IQ, and $X_5 =$ Interaction between GPA and Gender. Note: the data here is limited as gender was collected as a binary variable.

The response is starting salary after graduation (in thousands of dollars). Suppose we use least squares to fit the model and get $\hat{\beta}_0=50, \hat{\beta}_1=20, \hat{\beta}_2=0.07, \hat{\beta}_3=35, \hat{\beta}_4=0.01$, and $\hat{\beta}_5=-10$.

(a) Which answer is correct and why? [single choice question]

i. For a fixed value of IQ and GPA, males earn more on average than females.

ii. For a fixed value of IQ and GPA, females earn more on average than males.

iii. For a fixed value of IQ and GPA, males earn more on average than females provided that the GPA is high enough.

iv. For a fixed value of IQ and GPA, females earn more on average than males provided that the GPA is high enough.

6A) iii is correct because of the difference. If the GPA is low, females earn more, but if it is high enough then males earn more on average.

(b) Wite down the least square function and then predict the salary of a female with IQ of 110 and a GPA of 4.0.

In [133]:
#function for least squares to predict salary
def salary_prediction(gpa, iq, gender):
    beta_0 = 50
    beta_1 = 20
    beta_2 = 0.07
    beta_3 = 35
    beta_4 = 0.01
    beta_5 = -10

    gpa_iq = gpa * iq
    gpa_gender = gpa * gender

    salary = (beta_0 +
    beta_1 * gpa +
    beta_2 * iq +
    beta_3 * gender +
    beta_4 * gpa_iq +
    beta_5 * gpa_gender)

    return salary
In [135]:
#female prediction 
female_prd = salary_prediction(gpa= 4.0, iq= 110, gender= 1)
print(female_prd)

In this extra credit problem, you'll build a simple web scraper to collect and process text data. You'll write the code necessary to scrape lyrics for a desired artist. Your code should be structured such that one can easily execute your scraping functions for a given artist. There are three deliverables for this assignment:

  1. A set of functions necessary for scraping the lyrics of a specific artist.
  2. An example implementation of using your functions.
  3. A file of example output from your notebook implementation.

The specific approach that you take to structuring your code is up to you, but the final output .csv data should have the following columns (each row is a song from an artist that you choose):

  • Column 1: artist
  • Column 2: album
  • Column 3: song title
  • Column 4: URL of song lyrics
  • Column 5: song lyrics (all of the lyrics in one column)
  • Column 6: number of words in the song

Data Scraping: The actual scraping of data should be supported by separate functions that accomplish these tasks:

  1. Given an artist, identify all of their albums, songs, and links to songs.
  2. Given a set of song links (from step 1), collect the lyrics to each song and store them in a data frame.

In order to do this, you'll need to understand the structure of your lyrics site. The site you use is up to you, but all of this information should be available on lyrics.com.

Data Processing:
